intro: I am a student across every area on this page, and this page is deliberately honest about that. It tracks what I am actively studying, what I have tested in real projects, and what remains planned — so progress is visible without pretending to expertise I have not earned yet.

disciplines.title: AI & Machine Learning
disciplines.stance: Learning by fine-tuning and evaluating real models for Khmer, where low-resource constraints punish cargo-cult ML quickly.
currentFocus: Speech-model fine-tuning and feature pipelines (Whisper-family models)
Evaluation design for Khmer text, where character error rate beats word error rate
Error analysis by speaker, device, and noise condition
Writing model cards that state dataset provenance and failure modes

disciplines.title: Software & Product Systems
disciplines.stance: Learning to ship small, typed, tested systems instead of large unproven architectures.
currentFocus: Deterministic pipelines with unit tests and CI
Typed content architectures and schema validation
Static-site engineering, deployment workflows, and rollback thinking
AI-native development workflows with explicit human review gates

disciplines.title: Business & Strategy
disciplines.stance: Learning to test commercial assumptions in the field before writing code.
currentFocus: International business coursework — [OWNER_INPUT_REQUIRED: List the specific courses or modules you want named]
Unit economics of agricultural coordination (spoilage, payment timing, fulfillment)
Buyer-first validation instead of marketplace-first assumptions
Reading markets where operations matter more than software

disciplines.title: Governance & Commercial Rules
disciplines.stance: Learning how contracts, terms, and policies decide what AI systems may do — as a builder who reads the rules, not as a lawyer.
currentFocus: Contracts and terms of service for software and AI products
Data licensing, consent, and privacy for speech datasets
Risk assessment and human-approval design patterns
How AI governance frameworks translate into product decisions

experiments.title: Khmer ASR fine-tuning
experiments.question: Can a fully reproducible Whisper-small pipeline reach a usable Khmer character error rate with limited public data?

experiments.title: Auditable decision engine
experiments.question: Can farm-lot assembly be made fully auditable with deterministic code, designed failure cases, and human approval gates?

experiments.title: Buyer-first coordination
experiments.question: Can one recurring buyer order coordinate 30–100 smallholder commitments before harvest?

experiments.title: Governance review practice
experiments.question: Can a structured pre-launch review (data use, terms, oversight, risk) be demonstrated well enough to practice on real products?

items.text: Publish a model card for Kaskor ASR with dataset composition and known failure modes.
Deepen contracts and terms-of-service study through international business coursework.
Run one recurring-buyer pilot for Chomkar OrderLoop and record every commitment and exception.
Turn the demonstration governance review into a real review of one CHNAI LAB product before its release.
Publish evaluation results by speaker, province, device, and noise condition for Khmer ASR.
Write publicly about how contracts and policies shaped a real product decision I was part of.
